```rs
// What prediction.rs reads off the connection: equipment changes and which entity kind is a player.
use crate::game::Game;
use horizon_core::geometry::{Aabb, Vec3};
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct RemoteMotion {
    pub rendered: Vec3,
    pub server: Vec3,
    pub bounds: Aabb,
    pub update_interval: u32,
    pub floating: bool,
}

pub(crate) fn is_player(game: &Game<'_>, kind: i32) -> bool {
    game.remote.as_ref().and_then(|r| r.builtin.get("minecraft:entity_type")).and_then(|registry| registry.name(kind))
        == Some("minecraft:player")
}
pub(crate) fn equipment(
    game: &Game<'_>,
    packet: &horizon_protocol::packets::play::Clientbound,
) -> Option<(u32, Vec<(usize, Option<horizon_client::items::ItemStack>)>)> {
    let horizon_protocol::packets::play::Clientbound::SetEquipment(p) = packet else {
        return None;
    };
    Some((
        u32::try_from(p.id).ok()?,
        p.slots
            .iter()
            .filter(|(slot, _)| *slot < 2)
            .map(|(slot, stack)| (usize::from(*slot), game.to_stack(stack)))
            .collect(),
    ))
}
pub(crate) fn motion(game: &Game<'_>, id: u32) -> Option<RemoteMotion> {
    let remote = game.remote.as_ref()?;
    let mob = game.mobs.iter().find(|m| m.id == id)?;
    let tracked = remote.entities.get(&i32::try_from(id).ok()?)?;
    let [x, y, z] = tracked.position;
    let server = Vec3::new(x, y, z);
    let interval = horizon_client::lan::tracking::settings(&mob.kind.id).1;
    if interval == 0 || !server.is_finite() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(RemoteMotion {
        rendered: mob.position,
        server,
        bounds: mob.bounds(),
        update_interval: interval,
        floating: mob.extra.fall_flying
            || mob.fluids.in_water
            || mob.fluids.in_lava
            || mob.climbing
            || mob.no_gravity
            || mob.extra.mount.is_some(),
    })
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct LocalMotion {
    pub feet: Vec3,
    pub previous: Vec3,
    pub bounds: Aabb,
    pub floating: bool,
}
/// The native previous-tick field is old_position, NOT the most recent movement
/// record (multiple records may belong to one tick).
pub(crate) fn local_motion(game: &Game<'_>) -> Option<LocalMotion> {
    use horizon_core::position::BlockPos;
    use horizon_world::{
        climbing::{self, ClimbingWorld},
        registry::BlockStateId,
    };
    struct ReadClimb<'a, 'g>(&'a Game<'g>);
    impl ClimbingWorld for ReadClimb<'_, '_> {
        type Error = ();
        fn is_spectator(&mut self) -> Result<bool, ()> {
            Ok(self.0.player.as_ref().ok_or(())?.spectator)
        }
        fn block_position(&mut self) -> Result<BlockPos, ()> {
            Ok(BlockPos::containing(self.0.player.as_ref().ok_or(())?.position))
        }
        fn in_block_state(&mut self) -> Result<BlockStateId, ()> {
            let p = self.block_position()?;
            self.block_state(p)
        }
        fn is_fall_flying(&mut self) -> Result<bool, ()> {
            Ok(self.0.player.as_ref().ok_or(())?.fall_flying)
        }
        fn block_state(&mut self, p: BlockPos) -> Result<BlockStateId, ()> {
            if !self.0.world.loaded(p.x, p.z) {
                return Err(());
            }
            Ok(self.0.world.block(p.x, p.y, p.z))
        }
        fn set_last_climbable_position(&mut self, _: BlockPos) {} // Read-only forecast.
    }
    let p = game.player.as_ref()?;
    let climbing =
        if p.flying { false } else { climbing::on_climbable(&mut ReadClimb(game), &game.motion.climbing).ok()? };
    Some(LocalMotion {
        feet: p.position,
        previous: p.old_position,
        bounds: p.bounds(),
        // Native local LivingMotionWorld::no_gravity is always false.
        floating: p.fall_flying || p.fluids.was_touching_water || p.is_in_lava() || climbing || game.riding.is_some(),
    })
}
```

```rs
// What a preset leaves as it is: the menu's and the HUD's look, Panic and the Client modules.
pub(super) fn untouched(m: &Module) -> bool {
    m.category == Category::Client || matches!(m.name, "ClickGUI" | "HUD" | "Panic")
}

// A preset by its id or its title.
pub(super) fn find(name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let n = super::sunset::norm(name);
    PRESETS.iter().position(|p| super::sunset::norm(p.id) == n || super::sunset::norm(p.title) == n)
}
```

`mixins/sunset/press.rs`:

```rs
// A mouse press goes to the click GUI while it is open, before the game sees it; then to the Loadouts panel and
// Shulker Peek's view.
fn sunset_press(game: &mut crate::game::Game<'_>, button: winit::event::MouseButton) -> std::ops::ControlFlow<bool> {
    if crate::game::sunset::gui_open() {
        crate::game::sunset::gui_press(game, button);
        return std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(true);
    }
    if crate::game::sunset_loadouts::press(game, button == winit::event::MouseButton::Right) {
        return std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(true);
    }
    if crate::game::sunset_render::peek_press(game, button == winit::event::MouseButton::Middle) {
        return std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(true);
    }
    std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(())
}
```

`mixins/sunset/profile_menu.rs`:

```rs
// The list the Profiles module's row opens: the saved profiles, or (its Presets tab) the pre-made ones. A click, or
// the arrows and Enter, loads a saved one; a preset first shows what taking it turns on and off, with Apply and Back.
// Left and Right change tabs. The files are read when it opens and when one loads, never while drawing.
use super::{Game, sunset::{Shape, accent, panel_radius}};
use super::sunset_presets::PRESETS;

const ROW: f32 = 18.0;
// The list's title above it and the room under it.
const TOP: f32 = 25.0;
const BOTTOM: f32 = 22.0;
// A preview's lines, and its buttons' row.
const LINE: f32 = 11.0;
const BUTTONS: f32 = 30.0;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(super) enum Tab {
    Saved,
    Presets,
}

// What a click or a key in the menu asks for.
pub(super) enum Choice {
    Load(String),
    Preview(usize),
    Apply(usize),
}

// A preset's preview: its lines (text, colour), fitted to the menu's width when it was made.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(super) struct Preview {
    pub(super) preset: usize,
    pub(super) lines: Vec<(String, u32)>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub(super) struct Menu {
    pub(super) names: Vec<String>,
    pub(super) error: Option<String>,
    pub(super) tab: Tab,
    pub(super) preview: Option<Preview>,
    focus: usize,
    start: usize,
}

pub(super) fn width(w: f32) -> f32 {
    (w - 16.0).min(300.0)
}

fn frame(w: f32, h: f32, count: usize) -> [f32; 4] {
    let ww = width(w);
    let hh = (count.clamp(1, 10) as f32 * ROW + TOP + BOTTOM).min(h - 16.0);
    [(w - ww) / 2.0, (h - hh) / 2.0, ww, hh]
}

fn preview_frame(w: f32, h: f32, lines: usize) -> [f32; 4] {
    let ww = width(w);
    let hh = (lines as f32 * LINE + TOP + BUTTONS + 6.0).min(h - 16.0);
    [(w - ww) / 2.0, (h - hh) / 2.0, ww, hh]
}

// How many preview lines fit.
fn preview_rows(r: [f32; 4]) -> usize {
    ((r[3] - TOP - BUTTONS - 6.0) / LINE).max(1.0) as usize
}

// The preview's Apply and Back buttons.
fn buttons(r: [f32; 4]) -> ([f32; 4], [f32; 4]) {
    let (bw, bh) = (60.0, 16.0);
    let y = r[1] + r[3] - bh - 8.0;
    ([r[0] + r[2] - 2.0 * bw - 14.0, y, bw, bh], [r[0] + r[2] - bw - 8.0, y, bw, bh])
}

// The two tabs in the title row.
fn tabs(r: [f32; 4]) -> [([f32; 4], Tab, &'static str); 2] {
    let y = r[1] + 4.0;
    [([r[0] + r[2] - 140.0, y, 50.0, 15.0], Tab::Saved, "Saved"), ([r[0] + r[2] - 86.0, y, 56.0, 15.0], Tab::Presets, "Presets")]
}

// How many rows fit.
fn rows(r: [f32; 4]) -> usize {
    ((r[3] - TOP - BOTTOM) / ROW).max(1.0) as usize
}

fn inside(r: [f32; 4], at: (f32, f32)) -> bool {
    at.0 >= r[0] && at.0 < r[0] + r[2] && at.1 >= r[1] && at.1 < r[1] + r[3]
}

impl Menu {
    // On the saved profiles, or the presets when none is saved.
    pub(super) fn new(names: Vec<String>, selected: Option<&str>, w: f32, h: f32) -> Self {
        let tab = if names.is_empty() { Tab::Presets } else { Tab::Saved };
        let focus = selected.and_then(|n| names.iter().position(|p| p == n)).unwrap_or(0);
        let mut menu = Self { names, error: None, tab, preview: None, focus, start: 0 };
        menu.reveal(w, h);
        menu
    }

    fn count(&self) -> usize {
        match self.tab {
            Tab::Saved => self.names.len(),
            Tab::Presets => PRESETS.len(),
        }
    }

    fn rect(&self, w: f32, h: f32) -> [f32; 4] {
        match &self.preview {
            Some(p) => preview_frame(w, h, p.lines.len()),
            None => frame(w, h, self.count()),
        }
    }

    fn reveal(&mut self, w: f32, h: f32) {
        let count = rows(frame(w, h, self.count()));
        self.start = self.start.min(self.focus).max((self.focus + 1).saturating_sub(count));
    }

    fn switch(&mut self, tab: Tab, w: f32, h: f32) {
        if self.tab != tab {
            self.tab = tab;
            self.focus = 0;
            self.start = 0;
            self.error = None;
            self.reveal(w, h);
        }
    }

    // The row `i` of the tab shown: a profile to load or a preset to preview.
    fn choice(&self, i: usize) -> Option<Choice> {
        match self.tab {
            Tab::Saved => self.names.get(i).cloned().map(Choice::Load),
            Tab::Presets => (i < PRESETS.len()).then_some(Choice::Preview(i)),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn scroll(&mut self, steps: i32, w: f32, h: f32) {
        if self.preview.is_some() {
            return;
        }
        let max = self.count().saturating_sub(rows(frame(w, h, self.count())));
        self.start = (self.start as i32 + steps).clamp(0, max as i32) as usize;
    }

    // Esc: out of a preview (true), else the menu closes.
    pub(super) fn back(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.error = None;
        self.preview.take().is_some()
    }

    // Up and Down move the mark, Left and Right change tabs, Enter loads or previews (and in a preview, applies).
    pub(super) fn key(&mut self, key: &str, w: f32, h: f32) -> Option<Choice> {
        let enter = matches!(key, "key.keyboard.enter" | "key.keyboard.numpad.enter");
        if let Some(p) = &self.preview {
            return enter.then_some(Choice::Apply(p.preset));
        }
        match key {
            "key.keyboard.up" => self.focus = self.focus.saturating_sub(1),
            "key.keyboard.down" => self.focus = (self.focus + 1).min(self.count().saturating_sub(1)),
            "key.keyboard.left" => self.switch(Tab::Saved, w, h),
            "key.keyboard.right" => self.switch(Tab::Presets, w, h),
            _ if enter => return self.choice(self.focus),
            _ => return None,
        }
        self.reveal(w, h);
        None
    }

    // What a click asks for, if anything (a tab or Back is done here).
    pub(super) fn click(&mut self, at: (f32, f32), w: f32, h: f32) -> Option<Choice> {
        let r = self.rect(w, h);
        if let Some(p) = &self.preview {
            let (apply, back) = buttons(r);
            if inside(apply, at) {
                return Some(Choice::Apply(p.preset));
            }
            if inside(back, at) {
                self.back();
            }
            return None;
        }
        if let Some((_, tab, _)) = tabs(r).into_iter().find(|(t, _, _)| inside(*t, at)) {
            self.switch(tab, w, h);
            return None;
        }
        let list = [r[0] + 4.0, r[1] + TOP, r[2] - 8.0, rows(r) as f32 * ROW];
        inside(list, at).then(|| self.choice(self.start + ((at.1 - list[1]) / ROW) as usize)).flatten()
    }

    // A click outside the menu or on its x closes it.
    pub(super) fn closes(&self, at: (f32, f32), w: f32, h: f32) -> bool {
        let r = self.rect(w, h);
        !inside(r, at) || inside([r[0] + r[2] - 25.0, r[1], 25.0, 22.0], at)
    }
}

fn fit(game: &Game<'_>, text: &str, width: f32) -> String {
    super::sunset::fit_to(game, text, width)
}

// The preview's lines at the menu's width: the preset's about (its title is the head), then `lines` (what it turns on
// and off, and the settings count).
pub(super) fn preview_lines(game: &Game<'_>, w: f32, preset: usize, lines: &[String]) -> Vec<(String, u32)> {
    let room = width(w) - 16.0;
    let about = super::sunset::wrap(game, PRESETS[preset].about, room);
    let mut out: Vec<(String, u32)> = about.into_iter().map(|l| (l, 0x909090)).collect();
    for line in lines {
        let colour = if line.starts_with("Turns on") {
            accent()
        } else if line.starts_with("Turns off") {
            0xFF9090
        } else {
            0xFFFFFF
        };
        out.extend(super::sunset::wrap(game, line, room).into_iter().map(|l| (l, colour)));
    }
    out
}

pub(super) fn draw(game: &Game<'_>, w: f32, h: f32, at: (f32, f32), selected: Option<&str>, menu: Option<&Menu>, out: &mut Vec<Shape>) {
    let Some(menu) = menu else {
        return;
    };
    let r = menu.rect(w, h);
    out.push(Shape::Fill([0.0, 0.0, w, h], 0x8000_0000));
    out.push(Shape::Round(r, panel_radius(), 0xFF12_1214));
    out.push(Shape::Text("x".into(), [r[0] + r[2] - 15.0, r[1] + 7.0], 0xFFFFFF));
    if let Some(p) = &menu.preview {
        out.push(Shape::Head(fit(game, PRESETS[p.preset].title, r[2] - 40.0), [r[0] + 8.0, r[1] + 7.0], 0xFFFFFF));
        let fits = preview_rows(r);
        for (n, (line, colour)) in p.lines.iter().take(fits).enumerate() {
            let text = if n + 1 == fits && p.lines.len() > fits { format!("{line} ...") } else { line.clone() };
            out.push(Shape::Text(fit(game, &text, r[2] - 16.0), [r[0] + 8.0, r[1] + TOP + n as f32 * LINE], *colour));
        }
        let (apply, back) = buttons(r);
        for (b, label, colour) in [(apply, "Apply", 0xFF00_0000 | accent()), (back, "Back", 0xFF3A_3A3A)] {
            out.push(Shape::Round(b, panel_radius(), colour));
            let tw = game.native_text_width(label);
            out.push(Shape::Text(label.to_owned(), [b[0] + (b[2] - tw) / 2.0, b[1] + super::sunset::text_y(b[3])], 0xFFFFFF));
        }
        if let Some(error) = &menu.error {
            out.push(Shape::Text(fit(game, error, r[2] - 150.0), [r[0] + 8.0, r[1] + r[3] - 20.0], 0xFF9090));
        }
        return;
    }
    out.push(Shape::Head("Profiles".into(), [r[0] + 8.0, r[1] + 7.0], 0xFFFFFF));
    for (t, tab, label) in tabs(r) {
        if menu.tab == tab {
            out.push(Shape::Round(t, panel_radius(), 0xFF28_282C));
        }
        let tw = game.native_text_width(label);
        out.push(Shape::Text(label.to_owned(), [t[0] + (t[2] - tw) / 2.0, t[1] + 3.0], if menu.tab == tab { accent() } else { 0x909090 }));
    }
    if menu.tab == Tab::Saved && menu.names.is_empty() {
        out.push(Shape::Text("None saved yet: .profile save <name>".into(), [r[0] + 8.0, r[1] + TOP + 5.0], 0xFFFFFF));
    }
    for i in (menu.start..menu.count()).take(rows(r)) {
        let row = [r[0] + 4.0, r[1] + TOP + (i - menu.start) as f32 * ROW, r[2] - 8.0, ROW];
        if inside(row, at) || i == menu.focus {
            out.push(Shape::Round(row, panel_radius(), 0xFF28_282C));
        }
        let at_text = [row[0] + 5.0, row[1] + 5.0];
        match menu.tab {
            Tab::Saved => {
                let name = &menu.names[i];
                let colour = if selected == Some(name.as_str()) { accent() } else { 0xFFFFFF };
                out.push(Shape::Text(fit(game, name, row[2] - 10.0), at_text, colour));
            }
            Tab::Presets => {
                let preset = &PRESETS[i];
                let colour = if selected == Some(preset.id) { accent() } else { 0xFFFFFF };
                let title = fit(game, preset.title, row[2] - 10.0);
                let tw = game.native_text_width(&title);
                out.push(Shape::Text(title, at_text, colour));
                let room = row[2] - 18.0 - tw;
                if room > 30.0 {
                    out.push(Shape::Text(fit(game, preset.about, room), [at_text[0] + tw + 8.0, at_text[1]], 0x808080));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(error) = &menu.error {
        out.push(Shape::Text(fit(game, error, r[2] - 16.0), [r[0] + 8.0, r[1] + r[3] - 16.0], 0xFF9090));
    }
}
```

`mixins/sunset/profiles.rs`:

```rs
// Profiles as files: `<mod data>/profiles/<name>.profile`, with the checks from Rust's pull request #2 (names that
// are safe file names on every system, size limits, no links or junctions in the way, writes that leave the old file
// whole when they fail), a backup of the settings before every load, and export and import folders beside them. Only
// the mod's own data folder is ever written; no command names a path.

use std::fs::{self, File, OpenOptions};
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

pub(super) const HEADER: &str = "sunset-profile=1";
// The settings as they were before the last load.
pub(super) const BACKUP: &str = "before-load";
const MAX_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;
const MAX_PROFILES: usize = 128;

// Selection belongs to the config, never to a portable profile. Hashing is only
// change detection, not a trust check; the full module snapshot is canonical.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub(super) struct Selection {
    current: Option<(String, u64)>,
    before: Option<(String, u64)>,
    modified: bool,
}

fn fingerprint(text: &str) -> u64 {
    text.bytes().fold(0xcbf29ce484222325, |hash, byte| (hash ^ u64::from(byte)).wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3))
}

impl Selection {
    pub(super) fn refresh(&mut self, snapshot: &str) {
        self.modified = self.current.as_ref().is_some_and(|(_, hash)| *hash != fingerprint(snapshot));
    }
    pub(super) fn selected(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.current.as_ref().map(|(name, _)| name.as_str())
    }
    pub(super) fn label(&self) -> String {
        match self.selected() {
            Some(name) => format!("{name}{}", if self.modified { " (modified)" } else { "" }),
            None => "Custom".into(),
        }
    }
    pub(super) fn choose(&mut self, name: &str, snapshot: &str) {
        self.current = Some((name.to_owned(), fingerprint(snapshot)));
        self.modified = false;
    }
    pub(super) fn loaded(&mut self, name: &str, snapshot: &str) {
        let previous = self.current.clone();
        if name == BACKUP {
            self.current = self.before.take();
        } else {
            self.choose(name, snapshot);
        }
        self.before = previous;
        self.refresh(snapshot);
    }
    pub(super) fn deleted(&mut self, name: &str) {
        if self.selected() == Some(name) {
            self.current = None;
            self.modified = false;
        }
        if self.before.as_ref().is_some_and(|(n, _)| n == name) { self.before = None; }
    }
    pub(super) fn stored(&self) -> String {
        let encode = |value: &Option<(String, u64)>| value.as_ref().map_or(String::new(), |(n, h)| format!("{n}|{h:016x}"));
        format!("{};{}", encode(&self.current), encode(&self.before))
    }
    pub(super) fn restore(&mut self, text: &str) {
        let decode = |value: &str| -> Option<(String, u64)> {
            let (n, hash) = value.split_once('|')?;
            (name(n).ok()?.as_str() == n && n != BACKUP && hash.len() == 16)
                .then(|| u64::from_str_radix(hash, 16).ok().map(|h| (n.to_owned(), h))).flatten()
        };
        let (current, before) = text.split_once(';').unwrap_or(("", ""));
        self.current = decode(current);
        self.before = decode(before);
        self.modified = false;
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod selection_tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn edits_and_restores_are_tracked() {
        let mut s = Selection::default();
        s.choose("bedwars", "hud.on=true");
        s.refresh("hud.on=false");
        assert_eq!(s.label(), "bedwars (modified)");
        s.refresh("hud.on=true");
        assert_eq!(s.label(), "bedwars");
    }
    #[test]
    fn saved_selection_survives_restart_with_dirty_state() {
        let mut s = Selection::default();
        s.choose("smp", "baseline");
        let mut restored = Selection::default();
        restored.restore(&s.stored());
        restored.refresh("changed");
        assert_eq!(restored.label(), "smp (modified)");
    }
    #[test]
    fn undo_preserves_previous_name_and_dirty_baseline() {
        let mut s = Selection::default();
        s.choose("smp", "baseline");
        s.loaded("bedwars", "new");
        let mut restored = Selection::default();
        restored.restore(&s.stored());
        restored.loaded(BACKUP, "changed");
        assert_eq!(restored.label(), "smp (modified)");
        restored.loaded(BACKUP, "new");
        assert_eq!(restored.label(), "bedwars");
    }
    #[test]
    fn deleting_selected_profile_and_invalid_metadata_show_custom() {
        let mut s = Selection::default();
        s.choose("bedwars", "baseline");
        s.deleted("bedwars");
        assert_eq!(s.label(), "Custom");
        for text in ["../secret|0000000000000000;", "before-load|0000000000000000;", "bedwars|bad;", "broken"] {
            s.restore(text);
            assert_eq!(s.label(), "Custom");
        }
    }
}

// A profile's name as its file is called: 1 to 32 letters, digits, - or _, starting with a letter or digit, and not
// a name Windows keeps for itself.
pub(super) fn name(input: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let n = input.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().replace(' ', "-");
    let ok = !n.is_empty()
        && n.len() <= 32
        && n.as_bytes()[0].is_ascii_alphanumeric()
        && n.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'-' || b == b'_');
    if !ok {
        return Err("a name is 1 to 32 letters, digits, - or _, starting with a letter or digit".into());
    }
    let device = |p: &str| n.len() == 4 && n.starts_with(p) && n.as_bytes()[3].is_ascii_digit();
    if matches!(n.as_str(), "con" | "prn" | "aux" | "nul") || device("com") || device("lpt") {
        return Err(format!("{n} is a name Windows keeps for itself"));
    }
    Ok(n)
}

// A link or a Windows junction (a reparse point).
fn linked(m: &fs::Metadata) -> bool {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        use std::os::windows::fs::MetadataExt;
        m.file_attributes() & 0x400 != 0
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        m.file_type().is_symlink()
    }
}

fn plain(path: &Path, directory: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
    let m = fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(|e| format!("can't look at {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if linked(&m) || m.is_dir() != directory {
        return Err(format!("{} must be a plain {} (no links)", path.display(), if directory { "folder" } else { "file" }));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn folder(path: PathBuf) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    match fs::create_dir_all(&path) {
        Ok(()) => plain(&path, true).map(|()| path),
        Err(e) => Err(format!("can't make {}: {e}", path.display())),
    }
}

pub(super) struct Store {
    profiles: PathBuf,
    exports: PathBuf,
    imports: PathBuf,
}

impl Store {
    // The mod's data folder, from the game.
    pub(super) fn new(data: PathBuf) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let data = folder(data)?;
        Ok(Self { profiles: folder(data.join("profiles"))?, exports: folder(data.join("exports"))?, imports: folder(data.join("imports"))? })
    }

    pub(super) fn path(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.profiles.join(format!("{name}.profile"))
    }

    pub(super) fn exists(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.path(name).is_file()
    }

    pub(super) fn read(&self, name: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        read(&self.path(name))
    }

    // The saved profiles, less the backup.
    pub(super) fn list(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        let mut names = Vec::new();
        for entry in fs::read_dir(&self.profiles).map_err(|e| format!("can't list the profiles: {e}"))?.flatten() {
            let file = entry.file_name();
            if let Some(n) = file.to_str().and_then(|f| f.strip_suffix(".profile"))
                && name(n).as_deref() == Ok(n)
                && n != BACKUP
            {
                names.push(n.to_owned());
            }
        }
        names.sort();
        Ok(names)
    }

    pub(super) fn write(&self, name: &str, text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        if name != BACKUP && !self.exists(name) && self.list()?.len() >= MAX_PROFILES {
            return Err(format!("{MAX_PROFILES} profiles are the most; delete one first"));
        }
        write(&self.path(name), text)
    }

    pub(super) fn delete(&self, name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        let path = self.path(name);
        plain(&path, false)?;
        fs::remove_file(&path).map_err(|e| format!("can't delete {name}: {e}"))
    }

    // A copy in the exports folder, to share: where it went.
    pub(super) fn export(&self, name: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
        let to = self.exports.join(format!("{name}.profile"));
        write(&to, &self.read(name)?)?;
        Ok(to)
    }

    // A profile file someone put in the imports folder.
    pub(super) fn import(&self, name: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        read(&self.imports.join(format!("{name}.profile")))
    }

    // Another kind of file (a loadout) to share: written to the exports folder as `file`, where it went.
    pub(super) fn share(&self, file: &str, text: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
        let to = self.exports.join(file);
        write(&to, text)?;
        Ok(to)
    }

    // Such a file someone put in the imports folder.
    pub(super) fn shared(&self, file: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        read(&self.imports.join(file))
    }

    pub(super) fn imports(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.imports
    }
}

fn read(path: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    plain(path, false)?;
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    File::open(path)
        .and_then(|f| f.take(MAX_BYTES as u64 + 1).read_to_end(&mut bytes))
        .map_err(|e| format!("can't read {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if bytes.len() > MAX_BYTES {
        return Err("a profile is 1 MiB at most".into());
    }
    String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| "a profile is UTF-8 text".into())
}

// Written beside the old file and renamed over it, so a failed write leaves the old one whole.
fn write(path: &Path, text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    if text.len() > MAX_BYTES {
        return Err("a profile is 1 MiB at most".into());
    }
    if fs::symlink_metadata(path).is_ok() {
        plain(path, false)?;
    }
    let tmp = path.with_extension(format!("tmp{}", std::process::id()));
    let done = OpenOptions::new()
        .write(true)
        .create_new(true)
        .open(&tmp)
        .and_then(|mut f| f.write_all(text.as_bytes()).and_then(|()| f.sync_all()))
        .and_then(|()| fs::rename(&tmp, path));
    if done.is_err() {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
    }
    done.map_err(|e| format!("can't write {}: {e}", path.display()))
}
```

`mixins/sunset/pvp_bot.rs`:

```rs
// Sword PvP Bot, from Rust's PR #16 (its settings and what it does; written small here): fights the nearest enemy
// player with your sword by itself. It turns you towards them at a human pace, walks and sprints in, keeps its
// distance (Patient) or presses on (Aggressive), strafes, jumps for critical hits and on being hit (Jump reset), and
// eats a golden apple when low. Hits go through the strikes queue like Kill Aura's. Your own movement keys take over.
use super::sunset::{self, Category, Module, hold, own_id};
use super::sunset_util as util;
use super::{Game, Screen};
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::sync::Mutex;
use winit::event::MouseButton;
use winit::keyboard::KeyCode;

const NAME: &str = "Sword PvP Bot";
const KEYS: [KeyCode; 6] = [KeyCode::KeyW, KeyCode::KeyS, KeyCode::KeyA, KeyCode::KeyD, KeyCode::ControlLeft, KeyCode::Space];
// The vanilla reach to a player's box, with a little kept back.
const REACH: f64 = 2.9;

pub(super) fn defaults() -> Vec<Module> {
    vec![
        Module::new(NAME, Category::Combat, "Fights the nearest player.")
            .pick("Style", &["Patient", "Aggressive"])
            .num("Fight range", 16.0, 6.0, 32.0, 1.0)
            .num("Turn speed", 1.0, 0.5, 1.5, 0.05)
            .bool("Strafe", true)
            .bool("Jump crits", true)
            .bool("Jump reset", true)
            .num("Gapple below HP", 10.0, 0.0, 20.0, 1.0),
    ]
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Bot {
    // The keys the bot holds down (never one you hold yourself).
    pressed: HashSet<KeyCode>,
    // Strafing right (else left), and the tick it turns the other way.
    right: bool,
    flip_at: u64,
    // Eating: the slot to go back to.
    eating: Option<usize>,
    health: f32,
    // Ticks the hit has been ready for, on the ground, waiting for a jump to fall.
    ready_for: u32,
}

static BOT: Mutex<Option<Bot>> = Mutex::new(None);

fn bot<R>(f: impl FnOnce(&mut Bot) -> R) -> R {
    f(BOT.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).get_or_insert_with(Bot::default))
}

// Lets go of the keys the bot holds and stops eating.
pub(super) fn release(game: &mut Game<'_>) {
    let (pressed, eating) = bot(|b| (std::mem::take(&mut b.pressed), b.eating.take()));
    for key in pressed {
        if !game.physical_keys.contains(&key) {
            game.keys.remove(&key);
        }
    }
    if let Some(back) = eating {
        let _ = game.play_mouse(MouseButton::Right, false);
        hold(game, back);
    }
}

fn press(game: &mut Game<'_>, want: &[KeyCode]) {
    let before = bot(|b| std::mem::take(&mut b.pressed));
    let mut pressed = HashSet::new();
    for key in KEYS {
        if want.contains(&key) {
            game.keys.insert(key);
            pressed.insert(key);
        } else if before.contains(&key) && !game.physical_keys.contains(&key) {
            game.keys.remove(&key);
        }
    }
    bot(|b| b.pressed = pressed);
}

// Turns the view towards (yaw, pitch) by at most `step` degrees a tick.
fn turn(game: &mut Game<'_>, yaw: f32, pitch: f32, step: f32) {
    let dy = (yaw - game.yaw + 540.0).rem_euclid(360.0) - 180.0;
    game.yaw += dy.clamp(-step, step);
    game.pitch += (pitch - game.pitch).clamp(-step, step);
}

// Ground a step ahead along `dir`: a drop of more than 2 blocks, lava or fire there is no place to walk.
fn safe_ahead(game: &Game<'_>, dir: [f64; 2]) -> bool {
    let Some(p) = game.player.as_ref() else {
        return false;
    };
    let (x, z) = ((p.position.x + dir[0]).floor() as i32, (p.position.z + dir[1]).floor() as i32);
    let y = p.position.y.floor() as i32;
    let burns = |y: i32| {
        let name = &game.res.facts().get(game.world.block(x, y, z)).name;
        name.ends_with(":lava") || name.ends_with(":fire")
    };
    if burns(y) || burns(y - 1) {
        return false;
    }
    (1..=3).any(|d| !game.res.facts().is_air(game.world.block(x, y - d, z)))
}

pub(super) fn tick(game: &mut Game<'_>, mods: &[Module]) {
    let Some(m) = mods.iter().find(|m| m.name == NAME && m.on) else {
        if bot(|b| !b.pressed.is_empty() || b.eating.is_some()) {
            release(game);
        }
        return;
    };
    let live = game.remote.is_some()
        && game.screen == Screen::Playing
        && !sunset::gui_open()
        && !game.spectator()
        && game.player.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| p.health.health() > 0.0);
    // Your own movement keys: the bot lets go and waits.
    let yours = KEYS.iter().any(|k| game.physical_keys.contains(k));
    let me = own_id(game);
    let range = m.n("Fight range");
    let target = game
        .mobs
        .iter()
        .filter(|mob| Some(mob.id) != me && util::player_enemy(game, mob))
        .map(util::mob_target)
        .filter(|t| game.player.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| util::dist([p.position.x, p.position.y, p.position.z], t.pos) <= range))
        .min_by(|a, b| {
            let at = game.player.as_ref().map_or([0.0; 3], |p| [p.position.x, p.position.y, p.position.z]);
            util::dist(at, a.pos).total_cmp(&util::dist(at, b.pos))
        });
    let (Some(t), Some(eye), true, false) = (target, game.eye_position(), live, yours) else {
        release(game);
        return;
    };
    let Some(p) = game.player.as_ref() else {
        return;
    };
    let (health, ground, falling, in_water) = (
        p.health.health() + p.health.absorption(),
        p.ground.on_ground,
        !p.ground.on_ground && p.velocity.y < 0.0,
        p.fluids.was_touching_water,
    );
    let hurt = bot(|b| std::mem::replace(&mut b.health, health)) > health + 0.01;
    // A golden apple when low; the fight waits while it eats.
    let low = f64::from(health) < m.n("Gapple below HP");
    let eating = bot(|b| b.eating);
    match (eating, low) {
        (Some(_), true) => {
            press(game, &[KeyCode::KeyS]);
            if game.using.is_none() {
                let _ = game.play_mouse(MouseButton::Right, true);
            }
            return;
        }
        (Some(_), false) => release(game),
        (None, true) => {
            if let Some(slot) = util::find_held(game, |n| n.ends_with("golden_apple")) {
                let back = game.selected;
                press(game, &[KeyCode::KeyS]);
                hold(game, slot);
                let _ = game.play_mouse(MouseButton::Right, true);
                bot(|b| b.eating = Some(back));
                return;
            }
        }
        (None, false) => {}
    }
    if let Some(sword) = util::find_held(game, |n| n.ends_with("_sword"))
        && !game.held().is_some_and(|s| s.item.ends_with("_sword") || s.item.ends_with("_axe"))
    {
        hold(game, sword);
    }
    // Aim at the nearest point of their box to your eyes' height, turned to at Turn speed (40 degrees a tick at 1).
    let aim = [(t.lo[0] + t.hi[0]) / 2.0, eye[1].clamp(t.lo[1] + 0.2, t.hi[1] - 0.2), (t.lo[2] + t.hi[2]) / 2.0];
    let (yaw, pitch) = sunset::look_at(eye, aim);
    turn(game, yaw, pitch, 40.0 * m.n("Turn speed") as f32);
    let near = [(t.lo[0] - eye[0]).max(eye[0] - t.hi[0]).max(0.0), (t.lo[1] - eye[1]).max(eye[1] - t.hi[1]).max(0.0), (t.lo[2] - eye[2]).max(eye[2] - t.hi[2]).max(0.0)];
    let reach = (near[0] * near[0] + near[1] * near[1] + near[2] * near[2]).sqrt();
    let off = ((yaw - game.yaw + 540.0).rem_euclid(360.0) - 180.0).abs();
    let ready = game.hand_strength.scale(0.5, game.main_hand_attack_speed()) >= 1.0;
    // The hit: cooldown full, in reach and in view; with Jump crits, on the way down from a jump (or after 10 ticks
    // ready on the ground, so it never stalls).
    let ready_for = bot(|b| {
        b.ready_for = if ready && reach <= REACH && ground { b.ready_for + 1 } else { 0 };
        b.ready_for
    });
    let crit_ok = !m.b("Jump crits") || falling || in_water || ready_for > 10;
    if ready && reach <= REACH && off < 30.0 && crit_ok && !sunset::strike_waiting() {
        sunset::strike(game, t.id);
    }
    // Moving: in (sprinting) while out of reach; Patient backs off to 2.2 blocks while the cooldown fills, Aggressive
    // stays on them. Strafing turns the other way every 20 to 40 ticks.
    let mut want = Vec::new();
    let dir = [-(game.yaw.to_radians() as f64).sin(), (game.yaw.to_radians() as f64).cos()];
    let gap = util::dist([eye[0], 0.0, eye[2]], [t.pos[0], 0.0, t.pos[2]]);
    if gap > 3.0 || (m.p("Style") == "Aggressive" && gap > 1.5) {
        if safe_ahead(game, dir) {
            want.extend([KeyCode::KeyW, KeyCode::ControlLeft]);
        }
    } else if m.p("Style") == "Patient" && !ready && gap < 2.2 && safe_ahead(game, [-dir[0], -dir[1]]) {
        want.push(KeyCode::KeyS);
    }
    if m.b("Strafe") && gap < 6.0 {
        let now = game.ticks;
        let right = bot(|b| {
            if now >= b.flip_at {
                b.right = !b.right;
                b.flip_at = now + 20 + (now * 7919 % 21);
            }
            b.right
        });
        let side = if right { [-dir[1], dir[0]] } else { [dir[1], -dir[0]] };
        if safe_ahead(game, side) {
            want.push(if right { KeyCode::KeyD } else { KeyCode::KeyA });
        }
    }
    // A jump: for the critical hit as the cooldown comes round in reach, or as a hit lands (Jump reset).
    let soon = game.hand_strength.scale(0.5, game.main_hand_attack_speed()) >= 0.85;
    if ground && !in_water && ((m.b("Jump crits") && soon && reach <= REACH + 0.5) || (m.b("Jump reset") && hurt)) {
        want.push(KeyCode::Space);
    }
    press(game, &want);
}
```

`mixins/sunset/radar.rs`:

```rs
// Native-resolution player radar.
// Anubis (4ldenz) was a behavior reference.

use super::Game;
use super::sunset::{Category, Module, accent, own_id};
use super::sunset_radar_math::{
    circle_point, circle_segments, fitted_size, offset, pixel_width, project,
};
use horizon_client::extras::Corner;
use horizon_client::extras_hud::Corners;
use horizon_client::hud::HudBatch;

pub(super) fn defaults() -> Vec<Module> {
    vec![
        Module::new(
            "Radar",
            Category::Render,
            "Shows nearby players.",
        )
        .pick("Mode", &["Round", "Potato"])
        .num("Range", 64.0, 8.0, 256.0, 1.0)
        .num("Size", 100.0, 80.0, 320.0, 1.0)
        .bool("Rotate", true)
        .colour("Players color", "White"),
    ]
}

fn rgba(argb: u32) -> u32 {
    let [a, r, g, b] = argb.to_be_bytes();
    horizon_client::hud::rgba(r, g, b, a)
}

// Solid-atlas vector quads enter the existing HUD batch directly. The only
// edge fade is one physical pixel of coverage, not a blur or low-res texture.
fn band(
    game: &Game<'_>,
    batch: &mut HudBatch,
    center: [f32; 2],
    inner: f32,
    outer: f32,
    segments: usize,
    color: u32,
    feather: bool,
) {
    for i in 0..segments {
        let corners = [
            circle_point(center, inner, i, segments),
            circle_point(center, outer, i, segments),
            circle_point(center, outer, i + 1, segments),
            circle_point(center, inner, i + 1, segments),
        ];
        let start = batch.vertices.len();
        batch.fill_quad(&game.gui.atlas, corners, rgba(color));
        if feather {
            // fill_quad's two triangles use corners 0,1,2,0,2,3.
            for (vertex, corner) in batch.vertices[start..].iter_mut().zip([0, 1, 2, 0, 2, 3]) {
                if corner == 1 || corner == 2 {
                    vertex.color &= 0x00FF_FFFF;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn disc(game: &Game<'_>, batch: &mut HudBatch, center: [f32; 2], radius: f32, color: u32) {
    let pixel = pixel_width(batch.scale);
    let inner = (radius - pixel * 0.5).max(0.0);
    let segments = circle_segments(radius, batch.scale);
    // Two adjacent fan triangles share one quad; no temporary vertex vector.
    for i in (0..segments).step_by(2) {
        batch.fill_quad(
            &game.gui.atlas,
            [
                center,
                circle_point(center, inner, i, segments),
                circle_point(center, inner, i + 1, segments),
                circle_point(center, inner, i + 2, segments),
            ],
            rgba(color),
        );
    }
    band(
        game,
        batch,
        center,
        inner,
        radius + pixel * 0.5,
        segments,
        color,
        true,
    );
}

pub(super) fn draw(
    game: &Game<'_>,
    batch: &mut HudBatch,
    corners: &mut Corners,
    modules: &[Module],
) {
    let Some(module) = modules.iter().find(|m| m.name == "Radar" && m.on) else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(player) = game.player.as_ref() else {
        return;
    };
    if game.title.is_some() || !game.native_corner_shown(Corner::BottomLeft) {
        return;
    }
    let Some(size) = fitted_size(module.n("Size") as f32, batch.width, batch.height) else {
        return;
    };
    let (x, y) = corners.place(Corner::BottomLeft, size, size + 12.0);
    // A preceding native panel can consume the corner. Avoid drawing offscreen.
    if x < 0.0 || y < 2.0 || x + size > batch.width {
        return;
    }
    let center = [x + size / 2.0, y + size / 2.0];
    let radius = size / 2.0 - 1.0;
    let reach = radius - 17.0;
    let pixel = pixel_width(batch.scale);
    let rotate = module.b("Rotate");
    let yaw = f64::from(game.yaw);
    let range = module.n("Range");
    let alpha = game.clock.camera_fraction();
    let lerp = |previous: f64, current: f64| previous + alpha * (current - previous);
    let local = [
        lerp(game.previous_position.x, player.position.x),
        lerp(game.previous_position.z, player.position.z),
    ];
    let own = own_id(game);
    let color = module.c("Players color");
    // The players on it: where on the radar, from its middle.
    let dots = game
        .mobs
        .iter()
        .filter(|other| {
            other.kind.id == "minecraft:player"
                && Some(other.id) != own
                && other.alive()
                && !other.removed
                && !other.is_invisible()
                && !super::remote::sunset_radar_players::spectator(game, other.id)
        })
        .filter_map(|other| {
            let dx = lerp(other.previous.x, other.position.x) - local[0];
            let dz = lerp(other.previous.z, other.position.z) - local[1];
            project(dx, dz, yaw, rotate, range, reach - 3.0)
        });
    if module.p("Mode") == "Potato" {
        game.native_fill(batch, [x, y, size, size], 0xD016_1B24);
        for [ox, oy] in dots {
            game.native_fill(batch, [center[0] + ox - 2.0, center[1] + oy - 2.0, 4.0, 4.0], color);
        }
        game.native_fill(batch, [center[0] - 2.0, center[1] - 2.0, 4.0, 4.0], 0xFF00_0000 | accent());
        return;
    }
    // Keep the background fringe under the solid rim, so only one layer
    // contributes coverage at the outer device-pixel edge.
    disc(game, batch, center, radius - pixel, 0xD016_1B24);
    band(
        game,
        batch,
        center,
        radius - pixel * 1.5,
        radius - pixel * 0.5,
        circle_segments(radius, batch.scale),
        0xFF58_6371,
        false,
    );
    band(
        game,
        batch,
        center,
        radius - pixel * 0.5,
        radius + pixel * 0.5,
        circle_segments(radius, batch.scale),
        0xFF58_6371,
        true,
    );
    game.native_fill(
        batch,
        [center[0] - reach, center[1], reach * 2.0, pixel],
        0xFF35_3E49,
    );
    game.native_fill(
        batch,
        [center[0], center[1] - reach, pixel, reach * 2.0],
        0xFF35_3E49,
    );

    for (label, dx, dz) in [
        ("N", 0.0, -1.0),
        ("E", 1.0, 0.0),
        ("S", 0.0, 1.0),
        ("W", -1.0, 0.0),
    ] {
        let [ox, oy] = offset(dx, dz, yaw, rotate);
        let at = [
            center[0] + ox as f32 * (radius - 8.0) - game.native_text_width(label) / 2.0,
            center[1] + oy as f32 * (radius - 8.0) - 4.0,
        ];
        game.native_text(
            batch,
            label,
            at,
            if label == "N" { accent() } else { 0xC6CFD9 },
            true,
        );
    }

    let mut count = 0;
    for [ox, oy] in dots {
        let dot = [center[0] + ox, center[1] + oy];
        disc(game, batch, dot, 3.2, 0xFF09_0D13);
        disc(game, batch, dot, 2.3, color);
        count += 1;
    }
    disc(game, batch, center, 3.0, 0xFF00_0000 | accent());
    let [fx, fy] = if rotate {
        [0.0, -1.0]
    } else {
        let (sin, cos) = yaw.to_radians().sin_cos();
        [-sin as f32, cos as f32]
    };
    // Short heading marker distinguishes the local center from other players.
    for i in 4..8 {
        game.native_fill(
            batch,
            [
                center[0] + fx * i as f32 - 0.6,
                center[1] + fy * i as f32 - 0.6,
                1.2,
                1.2,
            ],
            0xFF00_0000 | accent(),
        );
    }
    let caption = format!("Radar  {range:.0}m  {count} players");
    game.native_text(batch, &caption, [x, y + size + 2.0], 0xC6CFD9, true);
}
```

`mixins/sunset/radar_math.rs`:

```rs
// Radar geometry for Horizon.

use std::sync::OnceLock;

const CIRCLE_POINTS: usize = 256;
static CIRCLE: OnceLock<[[f32; 2]; CIRCLE_POINTS]> = OnceLock::new();

// Physical pixels, not GUI pixels: edges stay one device pixel wide even
// with a fractional desktop scale or a large Minecraft GUI scale.
pub(super) fn pixel_width(scale: f32) -> f32 {
    if scale.is_finite() && scale > 0.0 {
        scale.recip()
    } else {
        1.0
    }
}

pub(super) fn circle_segments(radius: f32, scale: f32) -> usize {
    let physical_radius = f64::from(radius.max(0.0) / pixel_width(scale));
    // Bound the maximum chord error to a quarter of a device pixel for
    // supported window sizes, while keeping small markers inexpensive.
    [16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
        .into_iter()
        .find(|&segments| {
            physical_radius * (1.0 - (std::f64::consts::PI / segments as f64).cos()) <= 0.25
        })
        .unwrap_or(CIRCLE_POINTS)
}

pub(super) fn circle_point(center: [f32; 2], radius: f32, i: usize, segments: usize) -> [f32; 2] {
    let points = CIRCLE.get_or_init(|| {
        std::array::from_fn(|j| {
            let angle = std::f64::consts::TAU * j as f64 / CIRCLE_POINTS as f64;
            [angle.cos() as f32, angle.sin() as f32]
        })
    });
    let [x, y] = points[(i % segments) * (CIRCLE_POINTS / segments)];
    [center[0] + radius * x, center[1] + radius * y]
}

// North-up uses +X right, +Z down. Rotating puts the player's forward
// direction up (Minecraft yaw zero faces +Z).
pub(super) fn offset(dx: f64, dz: f64, yaw: f64, rotate: bool) -> [f64; 2] {
    if !rotate {
        return [dx, dz];
    }
    let (sin, cos) = yaw.to_radians().sin_cos();
    [-dx * cos - dz * sin, dx * sin - dz * cos]
}

pub(super) fn project(
    dx: f64,
    dz: f64,
    yaw: f64,
    rotate: bool,
    range: f64,
    radius: f32,
) -> Option<[f32; 2]> {
    if ![dx, dz, yaw, range, f64::from(radius)]
        .iter()
        .all(|n| n.is_finite())
        || range <= 0.0
        || radius <= 0.0
        || dx.hypot(dz) > range
    {
        return None;
    }
    let [x, y] = offset(dx, dz, yaw, rotate);
    Some([(x / range) as f32 * radius, (y / range) as f32 * radius])
}

pub(super) fn fitted_size(requested: f32, width: f32, height: f32) -> Option<f32> {
    // Four pixels of screen margin, twelve for the range label. Do not
    // rewrite the saved setting when temporarily fitting a small viewport.
    let size = requested.min(width - 4.0).min(height - 16.0).floor();
    (size.is_finite() && size >= 64.0).then_some(size)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn near(actual: [f32; 2], expected: [f32; 2]) {
        assert!(
            (actual[0] - expected[0]).abs() < 0.001,
            "{actual:?} != {expected:?}"
        );
        assert!(
            (actual[1] - expected[1]).abs() < 0.001,
            "{actual:?} != {expected:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn north_up_and_heading_up_match_minecraft_cardinal_yaws() {
        near(project(0., -24., 0., false, 48., 60.).unwrap(), [0., -30.]);
        near(project(24., 0., 90., false, 48., 60.).unwrap(), [30., 0.]);
        // Forward at yaw 0, 90, 180 and -90 must always appear above center.
        for (dx, dz, yaw) in [
            (0., 24., 0.),
            (-24., 0., 90.),
            (0., -24., 180.),
            (24., 0., -90.),
        ] {
            near(project(dx, dz, yaw, true, 48., 60.).unwrap(), [0., -30.]);
        }
        near(project(24., 0., 0., true, 48., 60.).unwrap(), [-30., 0.]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn range_is_horizontal_inclusive_and_rejects_invalid_coordinates() {
        near(project(48., 0., 0., false, 48., 60.).unwrap(), [60., 0.]);
        assert!(project(48.001, 0., 0., false, 48., 60.).is_none());
        assert!(project(40., 40., 0., true, 48., 60.).is_none());
        assert!(project(f64::NAN, 0., 0., false, 48., 60.).is_none());
        assert!(project(0., 0., f64::INFINITY, true, 48., 60.).is_none());
        assert!(project(0., 0., 0., false, 0., 60.).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn requested_size_fits_small_viewports_without_mutating_settings() {
        assert_eq!(fitted_size(150., 427., 240.), Some(150.));
        assert_eq!(fitted_size(320., 320., 180.), Some(164.));
        assert_eq!(fitted_size(150., 70., 100.), Some(66.));
        assert_eq!(fitted_size(150., 60., 100.), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn edge_width_is_one_physical_pixel_at_fractional_and_integer_gui_scales() {
        for scale in [0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 8.0] {
            assert!((pixel_width(scale) * scale - 1.0).abs() < 0.00001);
        }
        assert_eq!(pixel_width(f32::NAN), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(pixel_width(0.0), 1.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn circle_tessellation_tracks_device_resolution_with_bounded_chord_error() {
        for radius in [2.3, 3.0, 49.0, 74.0, 159.0] {
            for scale in [1.0, 1.25, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 8.0] {
                let segments = circle_segments(radius, scale);
                let error = f64::from(radius * scale)
                    * (1.0 - (std::f64::consts::PI / segments as f64).cos());
                assert!(error <= 0.25001, "{radius} at scale {scale}: {error}");
                assert!(segments <= 256 && segments >= 16 && segments.is_power_of_two());
            }
        }
        assert!(circle_segments(74.0, 3.0) > circle_segments(74.0, 1.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn cached_circle_vertices_are_closed_and_not_quantized_to_gui_scanlines() {
        near(circle_point([0., 0.], 10., 0, 64), [10., 0.]);
        near(circle_point([0., 0.], 10., 16, 64), [0., 10.]);
        near(circle_point([0., 0.], 10., 64, 64), [10., 0.]);
        let [x, y] = circle_point([0., 0.], 10., 1, 64);
        assert!((x.hypot(y) - 10.0).abs() < 0.00001);
        assert!((y - y.round()).abs() > 0.01);
    }
}
```

`mixins/sunset/recipes.rs`:

```rs
// Unlock All Recipes (World): the recipe book shows every recipe of Horizon's own recipe data as unlocked; it lives
// next to the book in recipe_book.rs. A server takes the book's place-recipe click only for recipes it put in your
// book, so a click on any other one lays it in the grid with ordinary slot clicks from your inventory instead.
use super::super::Game;
use horizon_client::menu::Input::{Pickup, QuickMove};
use horizon_protocol::packets::play::Clientbound as C;
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::sync::Mutex;

#[derive(Default)]
struct Book {
    // The displays the server put in your book, as its packets said.
    server: HashSet<i32>,
    // The client book's version once every display was in it (None: not shown, or shown no more).
    shown: Option<u64>,
}

static BOOK: Mutex<Option<Book>> = Mutex::new(None);

fn book<R>(f: impl FnOnce(&mut Book) -> R) -> R {
    f(BOOK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).get_or_insert_with(Book::default))
}

pub(crate) fn packet(packet: &C) {
    book(|b| match packet {
        C::Login(_) => b.server.clear(),
        C::RecipeBookAdd(p) => {
            if p.replace {
                b.server.clear();
            }
            b.server.extend(p.entries.iter().map(|e| e.id));
        }
        C::RecipeBookRemove(p) => {
            for id in &p.ids {
                b.server.remove(id);
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    });
}

// Each tick on a server: every display in the client's book while on; back to the server's own once off.
pub(crate) fn sync(game: &mut Game<'_>, on: bool) {
    if game.remote.is_none() {
        return;
    }
    let version = game.recipe_ui.client_version;
    if on {
        if book(|b| b.shown) == Some(version) {
            return;
        }
        game.ensure_book();
        let known: HashSet<i32> = game.recipe_ui.client.displays().into_iter().collect();
        let all: Vec<i32> = game.recipe_ui.book.as_ref().map_or_else(Vec::new, |b| b.entries.iter().map(|e| e.display_id).collect());
        let missing: Vec<i32> = all.into_iter().filter(|d| *d >= 0 && !known.contains(d)).collect();
        let ui = &mut game.recipe_ui;
        if !missing.is_empty() {
            for d in missing {
                ui.client.add(d);
            }
            ui.client_version += 1;
        }
        book(|b| b.shown = Some(ui.client_version));
    } else if book(|b| b.shown.take()).is_some() {
        let server = book(|b| b.server.clone());
        let ui = &mut game.recipe_ui;
        for d in ui.client.displays().into_iter().filter(|d| !server.contains(d)) {
            ui.client.remove(d);
        }
        ui.client_version += 1;
    }
}

// The book's click on entry `index`: true when it was not the server's to place, and the grid was filled here (the
// grid's items first go back to the inventory; each stack is picked up, one dropped in each cell that takes it, and
// put back).
pub(crate) fn place(game: &mut Game<'_>, index: usize) -> bool {
    if game.remote.is_none() || book(|b| b.shown.is_none()) {
        return false;
    }
    let Some(entry) = game.recipe_ui.book.as_ref().and_then(|b| b.entries.get(index)).cloned() else {
        return false;
    };
    if book(|b| b.server.contains(&entry.display_id)) {
        return false;
    }
    let size = match game.remote_menu().1.as_str() {
        "inventory" => 2,
        "minecraft:crafting" => 3,
        _ => return true,
    };
    if !entry.fits(size, size) {
        return true;
    }
    let mut ops = Vec::new();
    for cell in 0..size * size {
        if game.slot_mut(100 + cell).is_some() {
            ops.push((Some(100 + cell), 0, QuickMove));
        }
    }
    let needs = entry.requirements();
    let mut left: Vec<(usize, String, u32)> =
        (0..36).filter_map(|i| game.inventory[i].as_ref().map(|s| (i, s.item.to_string(), s.count))).collect();
    let mut from: Vec<(usize, Vec<usize>)> = Vec::new();
    for (need, cell) in entry.grid_cells(size, size) {
        let Some(need) = need.and_then(|n| needs.get(n)) else {
            continue;
        };
        // A stack already being used for this kind first, so fewer pick-ups.
        let pick = left
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, (_, item, count))| *count > 0 && need.0.contains(item))
            .min_by_key(|(_, (slot, _, _))| !from.iter().any(|f| f.0 == *slot))
            .map(|(i, _)| i);
        let Some(i) = pick else {
            super::super::sunset::say(game, "Unlock All Recipes: not enough items for that recipe.");
            return true;
        };
        left[i].2 -= 1;
        let slot = left[i].0;
        match from.iter_mut().find(|f| f.0 == slot) {
            Some(f) => f.1.push(cell),
            None => from.push((slot, vec![cell])),
        }
    }
    for (slot, cells) in from {
        ops.push((Some(slot), 0, Pickup));
        ops.extend(cells.into_iter().map(|cell| (Some(100 + cell), 1, Pickup)));
        ops.push((Some(slot), 0, Pickup));
    }
    game.remote_menu_ops(&ops);
    true
}
```

```rs
// Unlock All Recipes: a click on a recipe the server has not given you lays it in the grid with slot clicks instead.
fn sunset_place_recipe(game: &mut crate::game::Game<'_>, entry_index: usize) -> std::ops::ControlFlow<()> {
    if crate::game::recipe_book::sunset_recipes::place(game, entry_index) {
        std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(())
    } else {
```

`mixins/sunset/remote_seq.rs`:

```rs
// Things Sunset needs from the connection's private state.
use crate::game::Game;

// The game's own sequence counter (the server wants block-action sequence
// numbers that never go down), for Sunset's placing and breaking.
pub(crate) fn next(game: &mut Game<'_>) -> i32 {
    game.next_sequence()
}

// A right click for the tick's keybind pass (Minecraft's keyUse.consumeClick): it waits for no use delay, and the
// game places with its own sequence number and prediction, before the tick's movement. Scaffold's Godbridge.
pub(crate) fn press_use(game: &mut Game<'_>) {
    if let Some(r) = game.remote.as_mut() {
        r.input.press(horizon_client::interaction_input::Button::Use);
    }
}

// The held slot as the server knows it: true when `slot` is news to it (the caller sends the SetCarriedItem). The
// game's tick sends one whenever the selection differs from what it last told, so this keeps it from sending the same
// slot a second time (Grim BadPacketsA, Intave "sent slot twice"). False without a connection.
pub(crate) fn tell_carried(game: &mut Game<'_>, slot: usize) -> bool {
    game.remote.as_mut().is_some_and(|r| r.carried.replace(slot) != Some(slot))
}

// The wait the game puts between one block's breaking and the next (5 ticks).
pub(crate) fn clear_destroy_delay(game: &mut Game<'_>, wait: u32) {
    if let Some(r) = game.remote.as_mut() {
        r.destroy_delay = r.destroy_delay.min(wait);
    }
}

// The block being broken by hand and how far it is (0 to 1), for Speed Mine.
pub(crate) fn breaking(game: &Game<'_>) -> Option<([i32; 3], f32)> {
    game.remote.as_ref()?.destroying.map(|(pos, _, done)| (pos, done))
}

pub(crate) fn set_breaking(game: &mut Game<'_>, done: f32) {
    if let Some((_, _, d)) = game.remote.as_mut().and_then(|r| r.destroying.as_mut()) {
        *d = done;
    }
}

// No Break Reset: the item in hand is no longer the one the break began with (the game would start it again).
pub(crate) fn breaking_item_changed(game: &Game<'_>) -> bool {
    game.remote.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| r.destroying.is_some() && r.destroying_item != game.main_hand_key())
}

// ...so the break goes on with the new one.
pub(crate) fn keep_breaking(game: &mut Game<'_>) {
    let held = game.main_hand_key();
    if let Some(r) = game.remote.as_mut() {
        r.destroying_item = held;
    }
}

// Anti Vanish: the names in the tab list (the listed players, not you).
pub(crate) fn tab_names(game: &Game<'_>) -> Vec<String> {
    game.remote.as_ref().map_or_else(Vec::new, |r| {
        r.tab_players.values().filter(|p| p.uuid != r.profile && r.listed.contains(&p.uuid)).map(|p| p.name.clone()).collect()
    })
}
```

```rs
struct Fc {
    pos: [f64; 3],
    prev: [f64; 3],
    yaw: f32,
```
